issue.title: Disconnect multidrone
issue.body:
How do I determine which drone corresponds to which ConnectionHandle?
I have multiple drones connected, and I need to identify which connection it belongs to in order to unsubscribe from its callbacks, and then if such a request is sent again, subscribe again.

comments.body: Can you keep track of it yourself using a `std::unordered_map` for instance?
How do I then get which address the drone is connected to?
Don't know, doesn't that depend on your setup?
My task is to bind the udpout://127.0.0.1:14550 endpoint to the handle of the drone that will be provided to us upon connection. Then, locate this drone by its udpout://127.0.0.1:14550 argument
So your drone talks on localhost? Is this PX4 SITL?
It doesn't matter. I have one drone connected to SITL and a second one that's real.
I'm sorry I don't have enough context to help you. You have to explain it in more detail, maybe add a diagram or show a source excerpt.

I am making a connection
add_any_connection_with_handle(connectionUrl);
let connectionUrl be: "udpin://0.0.0.0:14550".
Drones with IP addresses 127.0.0.2, 127.0.0.3, 127.0.0.4 are connected to it.
I need to disconnect the drone 127.0.0.3.

Ok, so you have to get the handle and use that to disconnect it. If you don't know which connection belongs to which drone, you need to keep track of it, as you create the connections.

E.g. add one connection: discover/collect drone on that connection and save connection handle and drone id to some structure (like a map), then add the next connection ...
What if I've created 3 connections and only three drones connected to the second one?
Well, then it's a map to a list of drones?

yes.
So I have 3 connections:

udpin://0.0.0.0:14550
udpin://0.0.0.0:15550
udpin://0.0.0.0:16550
After creating the connection, 3 drones connected: 127.0.0.2, 127.0.0.3, 127.0.0.4 to second connection (udpin://0.0.0.0:15550)
After a minute, I need to disconnect drone 127.0.0.3.

example 
main()
{
    add_any_connection_with_handle("udpin://127.0.0.1:14550"); //10.0.10.10
    add_any_connection_with_handle("udpin://127.0.0.1:15550"); //127.0.0.2, 127.0.0.3, 127.0.0.4
    add_any_connection_with_handle("udpin://127.0.0.1:16550"); ///10.0.10.20
    sleep(1000ms); //drone connected here
    remove_conection(drone_id); //the right drone should be here. which exists on the second connection. let's say 127.0.0.3
}
You can't disconnect a drone. You can only remove a connection. And you can ignore a drone if you don't create a system for it.
Can I find out his IP address?
It's only exposed via the debug print line.

mavlink协议 是通过 ID 进行区分
一个无人机，在系统中是一个 system，通过system id进行区分
同一个无人的多个功能模块例如照相、gps，通过component id进行区分，不管有多少个connection，都将给更新同一个system。
这些id都在无人机固件中配置的

Translation:
The MAVLink protocol distinguishes a single drone by ID. In the system, a drone is considered one "system," identified by a system ID. Multiple functional modules within the same drone — such as the camera and GPS — are distinguished by component ID. Regardless of how many connections there are, they all update the same system. These IDs are all configured in the drone's firmware.
